title: Compose the scheduler release kernel so a lease can durably reach RELEASED
description:
Objective: make `leaseState === "RELEASED"` reachable in durable daemon state by composing the release authority that already exists, and retire the daemon's duplicate of a design-765 rule that it never should have owned.

TWO MEASURED FACTS, both at HEAD a42ae2f.

FACT 1 — THE KERNEL EXISTS AND NOTHING CALLS IT. `releaseWork` at `packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:194` IS the design-765 release authority. It fences authority, treats an already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease as `NO_OP`, refuses a malformed request or an uncommittable handoff BEFORE composing any transition, and then splits three ways on `safeBoundaryObserved && effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal`: unsettled returns `outcome: "DRAINING"` with the lease at `DRAINING` and `resumable: false`; settled returns `outcome: "RELEASED"` with `lease.state === "RELEASED"`, the parsed `ReleaseHandoff`, the composed `DrainDisposition` and `resumable: disposition.resumable`. `grep -rn "releaseWork" apps` returns ZERO callers.

FACT 2 — THE SCHEDULER ROOT PUBLISHES NONE OF IT. A compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon importing from `@moe/scheduler`, typechecked and deleted in one command, returned errors for EVERY release symbol: TS2724 for `LEASE_STATES` ("Did you mean 'LeaseState'?") and TS2305 for `releaseWork`, `applyDrainReason`, `parseDisposition`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest` and `ReleaseResult`. `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:109` exports `SLOT_STATES` and the `LeaseState` type and nothing else from this family. A root-barrel grep is not evidence here; re-run the probe.

WHY THIS IS ALSO A CORRECTION, NOT ONLY AN ADDITION. task-740924b7 landed `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts` (249 lines, DONE and QA-approved) which validates a drain disposition through `@moe/runner`'s `parseDrainDisposition` / `isMonotonicDisposition` and then DERIVES `resumable` itself at :170 via a local `isResumable(disposition)`. That was correct against the surface available at the time and its values agree with the scheduler's today — but `@moe/scheduler`'s `DrainDisposition` (lease-drain.ts:31-38) ALREADY CARRIES `resumable`, computed by `composeDisposition` under the design-765 comment "only an unchanged strongest `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` stays resumable". The daemon now holds a second definition of that rule. The module's own header warns of exactly this: "two definitions would drift and core's release predicate would start refusing silently." Note also that the runner's `DrainDisposition` has NO `resumable` member while the scheduler's does, and core's `ExpansionReleaseEvidence.disposition` is `{resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget}` — the scheduler's shape, not the runner's.

Deliverable, in order: (1) publish the release family from `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts`; (2) call `releaseWork` from the daemon's attempt release path; (3) persist its `ReleaseResult` onto the existing durable row so `leaseState` carries the kernel's answer instead of the activation-time snapshot; (4) delete the local `isResumable` and take `resumable` from the returned disposition.

NOT in scope: the provider-slot release transition (task-4731ba34 — `releaseWork` does not touch slots), the terminal effect/resource refs, the safe-boundary observation, the `{digest, ref}` handoff projection (task-af9454f4, whose durable source is now this task's `ReleaseHandoff`), or the evidence reader (task-e62e3828).

Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/index.ts, apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts and its test, and the daemon call site.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — four legs, exit codes captured SEPARATELY, and read each `Test Files N passed` count line rather than the exit code.
definitionOfDone: The release family is reachable from the `@moe/scheduler` package ROOT: the same compiled bare-specifier probe that returned TS2305/TS2724 for `releaseWork`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest`, `ReleaseResult`, `applyDrainReason` and `parseDisposition` now typechecks clean, and the probe is deleted in the same command. Record the before and after output.

A lease durably reaches `RELEASED`: an end-to-end test drives the daemon release path with a settled boundary and reads `leaseState === "RELEASED"` back FROM DURABLE BYTES, where before this task the recorded value was the activation-time `ACTIVE` and `RELEASED` was unreachable.

The DRAINING branch is proven separately and is not collapsed into the released one: with `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` or `resourcesTerminal` false, the durable row records the DRAINING outcome and `resumable: false`, and a test asserts it differs from the released row field by field.

`resumable` comes from the kernel, not from the daemon: the local `isResumable` helper is DELETED, `grep -rn "isResumable" apps/daemon/src` returns zero, and the recorded value is the `disposition.resumable` the scheduler returned.
An already-RELEASED or REVOKED lease records the kernel's `NO_OP` outcome rather than a refusal or a second release row, and a test pins that a replay leaves exactly one durable row.

A mutation that makes the daemon derive `resumable` locally again, and separately one that records the activation-time lease state instead of the kernel's, each turn a NAMED test red; record both test names.

All four gate legs run with exit codes captured separately, both test legs print a nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Depends on the boundary and terminal facts: `releaseWork`'s ReleaseRequest requires `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal`, which are task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781. Until those land, drive them from the test as INPUTS to the kernel; never let the daemon assert them as durable truth on its own.
No caller-supplied lease state, disposition, truth class or handoff may become authority. The kernel decides; the daemon persists what it decided. Missing or unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN.
Use public package roots across package boundaries; the first step is the root export, not a deep import. Widen `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` only by the symbols this task actually consumes.

Exact codes and layers on every refusal path, positive generated counts on any sweep, target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400. attempt-release-disposition.ts is at 249 today, so this task must split it rather than grow it.

implementationPlan.description: Split the durable half out first, so the composition has room to land. `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts` is at 249 physical lines against a 250 target — one line of headroom — so this task MUST split it rather than grow it. Move the storage half into a new `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-store.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (every sibling in this directory has a git-tracked bridge; without it the module is invisible at runtime while tsc and vitest stay green): `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId` (:88), `durableActivation` (:133), `sameActivation` (:145), `releaseRecordBody` (:162), `commitRelease` (:185) and `readAttemptRelease` (:229). The composition half — the frozen vocabulary, `admitRequest`, `recordAttemptRelease` — stays. This is a pure move: no behaviour change, no renamed export, and the existing test file must pass untouched at the end of this step. Run the daemon test leg here to prove that before continuing; a split that quietly changed behaviour is far cheaper to find now than after the composition lands on top of it.

TDD the composition. In `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts`, write RED cases against a `recordAttemptRelease` that now calls `releaseWork`. (a) RELEASED: a settled boundary (`safeBoundaryObserved && effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal` all true) records `leaseState === "RELEASED"` read back FROM DURABLE BYTES — state the plain fact in the test name that before this task the recorded value was the activation-time `ACTIVE` and `RELEASED` was unreachable in the whole repo. (b) DRAINING, proven separately and never collapsed into (a): with any ONE of the three false, the row records the DRAINING outcome with `resumable: false`, and the test asserts it differs from the released row FIELD BY FIELD rather than merely "is not released". Drive all three false-one-at-a-time variants and assert the generated case count is 3. (c) NO_OP: a lease already `RELEASED` or `REVOKED` records the kernel's no-op, and a replay leaves EXACTLY ONE durable row — count the rows out of the store, since "it did not throw the second time" is also what a double write looks like. (d) `resumable` comes from the kernel: assert the recorded value equals the `disposition.resumable` the scheduler returned, and add a case where a caller-supplied `resumable` in the request payload contradicts it and loses.

Wire `releaseWork` and retire the daemon's duplicate rule. In `attempt-release-disposition.ts`, build the `AuthorityProof` `releaseWork` fences against — `{leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, expectedVersion, authorityHashRef}` — entirely from the RE-READ committed activation's `record.lease`, which carries every one of those fields; a caller-supplied proof is never consulted. Pass the `ReleaseRequest` through and let the kernel decide: it already runs `applyDrainReason(parsed.disposition, parsed.reason)` internally, so the daemon stops parsing or judging the disposition itself. DELETE the local `isResumable` at :158 and take `resumable` from the returned `disposition` — `grep -rn "isResumable" apps/daemon/src` must return zero. WATCH FOR A NEWLY UNREACHABLE CODE, which is the real hazard of this step: once the daemon no longer calls `@moe/runner`'s `parseDrainDisposition` / `isMonotonicDisposition`, any member of the frozen `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_CODES` that only that path could raise becomes unreachable while its test keeps passing against a hand-built input. For each code, either carry the kernel's own rejection (its `issues[0].code` and `.message`, surfaced unchanged) or REMOVE the code from the frozen list and from the vocabulary test in the same commit. Do not leave a dead member. Leave the runner-surface exports that task-740924b7 added in place; they are simply no longer imported here.

Feed the boundary facts as INPUTS, never as daemon-asserted truth, and keep the call site honest. `releaseWork`'s `ReleaseRequest` requires `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal`, whose durable producers are task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781 and are NOT landed — both are BLOCKED. Until they land, those three arrive on the request and the daemon passes them through to the kernel unmodified; it must never synthesize, default, or optimistically upgrade any of them, and it must not record them as durable truth of its own. Add a test asserting that a request omitting any of the three is refused rather than defaulted to false-and-released or true-and-released. In `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts` (213 lines against a 250 target — budget about ten lines) keep the existing call site shape and adjust only what the new signature requires. Record in a comment, with the two task ids, that the three flags are pass-through inputs pending their producers, so the next reader does not mistake a pass-through for a proven fact.

Single verification gate, four legs, exit codes captured SEPARATELY — a `&&` chain that dies at leg one hides every later count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Both package names resolve and both declare both scripts (verified at plan time: `@moe/scheduler` is packages/scheduler, `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon). READ THE OUTPUT, not the exit code — `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 for a package absent from the workspace, and the only discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line; record the nonzero count for BOTH test legs. The scheduler legs are non-negotiable here: step 1 edits `index.ts` and its roster guards, and a daemon-only gate would never see them. Daemon gates can be red at baseline from foreign in-flight slices — apply the path-attributed baseline (merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with owned paths must be EMPTY) and disclose any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines rather than hiding it or fabricating green.

Mutation drills and adversarial review, then stop. THREE drills, each restored before the next, each naming the test that reddens: (i) make the daemon derive `resumable` locally again instead of reading it off the kernel's disposition — the step-4(d) case must redden, which is what proves the duplicate rule is really gone rather than merely renamed; (ii) record the activation-time `record.lease.state` instead of the state on the lease the kernel returned — the step-4(a) RELEASED case must redden; (iii) collapse the DRAINING branch into the released one by ignoring the kernel's `outcome` field — the step-4(b) field-by-field comparison must redden. A drill that reddens the WRONG test, or that hangs, is not a pass. Drills run in a SHARED worktree: snapshot each file's hash before mutating and restore by content, never `git checkout`, and never trust `git status` to prove a revert — a peer's completion hook can commit a whole tree and swallow the drill while the tree reads clean. Then run the `adversarial-self-review` skill over the diff: two concurrent releases against one attempt aggregate; an activation whose `lease` is missing or whose counters sit at `MAX_AUTHORITY_COUNT` (which `fenceAuthority` refuses as an exhausted counter); a request whose `intentRefs` is empty; and per-file line counts — both halves of the split under 250 and foundation-attempt-service.ts still under 250.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
COMPOSE THE EXISTING KERNEL RATHER THAN EXTEND THE DAEMON'S OWN LOGIC. task-740924b7 shipped `attempt-release-disposition.ts` validating a disposition through `@moe/runner`'s `parseDrainDisposition` / `isMonotonicDisposition` and deriving `resumable` locally. That was the correct call against the surface visible at the time — but it was planned before `releaseWork` was found, and the runner's `DrainDisposition` has NO `resumable` member while the scheduler's does. Continuing down the runner path would mean the daemon permanently owning a copy of design 765. Rejected.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: reverting the runner-surface exports that 740924b7 added to `packages/runner/src/surface/recovery-surface.ts`. They are harmless once unused, another consumer may want them, and un-exporting churns the runner roster guards for no behavioural gain. The plan leaves them and simply stops importing them in the daemon.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: keeping the daemon's disposition pre-validation as defence in depth in front of `releaseWork`. That is two validators for one question and reintroduces exactly the drift this task exists to remove. `releaseWork` already refuses a malformed request and an incoherent disposition before composing any transition, and it refuses an uncommittable handoff BEFORE any state change, so authority is left as found.

SPLIT BEFORE COMPOSE, as its own step. attempt-release-disposition.ts is at 249 lines of a 250 target. Doing the split as a pure move with the existing suite green is what makes the composition reviewable; doing both at once produces a diff where a behaviour change hides inside a move.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD a42ae2f.

THE KERNEL. `releaseWork(record, authority, request)` at packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:194. It calls `fenceAuthority(record, authority, "releaseWork", RELEASE_STATES)` where `RELEASE_STATES` is ALL FIVE lease states (:89-91) with the comment "Terminal states are legal here so a repeat release is an idempotent no-op". Then: already RELEASED or REVOKED -> `accept({outcome: "NO_OP", lease, releasePending: false})`; malformed request -> `malformed`; unparseable handoff -> `malformed`; `applyDrainReason` failure -> carried; then `settled = safeBoundaryObserved && effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal`; unsettled -> `outcome: "DRAINING"`, lease at DRAINING with version+1, `resumable: false`, `releasePending: true`, `intentRefs`; settled -> `outcome: "RELEASED"`, lease at RELEASED with version+1, the parsed `ReleaseHandoff`, the composed `DrainDisposition`, and `resumable: disposition.resumable`. `grep -rn "releaseWork" apps` returns ZERO callers.

THE PROOF IS CONSTRUCTIBLE FROM DURABLE BYTES, which is what makes this composition legal. `parseProof` (lease-fencing.ts:51) requires `{leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, expectedVersion, authorityHashRef}`. `LeaseRecord` (authority-kernel.ts:83-95) carries leaseToken, epoch, ownerSessionRef, authorityHashRef, state and version. The daemon's re-read `ActivationLedgerRecord.lease` therefore supplies every field; nothing has to come from a caller. `fenceAuthority` also refuses when `version` or `epoch` reaches `MAX_AUTHORITY_COUNT`, as an exhausted-counter `malformed`, carrying no security event.

SHAPES. `ReleaseRequest {reason, safeBoundaryObserved, effectsTerminal, resourcesTerminal, handoff, intentRefs, disposition}` (:53-61, REQUEST_KEYS at :83). `ReleaseHandoff {completedSteps, activeProcessResourceFacts, inputDigest, worktreeDigest, contextDigest, journalDigest, artifactDigest, nextSafeAction, truthClass}` (HANDOFF_KEYS :79). Scheduler `DrainDisposition {reasons, strongestReason, terminalTarget, resumable}` (:31-38) - note `resumable`, absent from the runner's same-named type, and matching core's `ExpansionReleaseEvidence.disposition` shape.

THE ROOT IS EMPTY OF ALL OF IT. Compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon, typechecked and deleted in one command: TS2724 for `LEASE_STATES` ("Did you mean 'LeaseState'?") and TS2305 for `releaseWork`, `applyDrainReason`, `parseDisposition`, `DrainDisposition`, `ReleaseHandoff`, `ReleaseRequest`, `ReleaseResult`. `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:109` exports `SLOT_STATES` and nothing else from this family; its style is grouped `export { ... } from "./authority/<module>.js";` blocks.

ROSTER GUARDS. packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts pins `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` to 92 (:146), a sorted-key equality against `Object.keys(scheduler).sort()` (:251), and a per-export kind assertion (:254) driven by `[name, ExportKind]` pairs. Three assertions, all hand-transcribed.

THE LANDED DAEMON MODULE, 249 lines: vocabulary and layer at :40-60, `AttemptReleaseRequest` :74, `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId` :88, `coherenceRefusal` :103, `emittedReasons` :115, `admitRequest` :118, `durableActivation` :133, `sameActivation` :145, `isResumable` :158, `releaseRecordBody` :162, `commitRelease` :185, `recordAttemptRelease` :207, `readAttemptRelease` :229. Its own header already warns that "two definitions would drift and core's release predicate would start refusing silently" - which is precisely the condition this task repairs.

BRIDGES ARE MANDATORY in apps/daemon/src/work/; every sibling has a git-tracked one-line `.js`.

GATES RESOLVE: `@moe/scheduler` is packages/scheduler and `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, both with typecheck and test scripts.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE NEWLY UNREACHABLE REFUSAL CODE. Once the daemon stops calling the runner's disposition validators, any member of the frozen `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_CODES` that only that path could raise is dead - and its test keeps passing, because the test hands the refusal helper a hand-built input rather than driving production into that state. Audit every member against a real driving path; carry the kernel's own rejection or delete the member and its vocabulary entry in the same commit. A dead code in a frozen list is worse than no code: it reads as coverage.
2. THE THREE BOUNDARY FLAGS ARE NOT PROVEN FACTS YET. `safeBoundaryObserved`, `effectsTerminal` and `resourcesTerminal` have no durable producer - task-ded026d6 and task-6d400781 are both BLOCKED, each on further prerequisites. They pass through to the kernel as inputs and MUST NOT be synthesized, defaulted or upgraded by the daemon. A worker who defaults them to true to make the RELEASED test pass has manufactured the safe boundary the whole epic exists to prove.
3. The DRAINING branch is easy to lose. It returns `ok: true` with a different outcome, so a test asserting only "did not refuse" passes for both branches. Compare field by field, and drive all three unsettled variants rather than one.
4. `fenceAuthority` refuses an exhausted counter as MALFORMED, not as a state problem. A daemon test that seeds a lease near `MAX_AUTHORITY_COUNT` will get a surprising code; that is correct kernel behaviour, not a bug to route around.
5. Both roster-guard files live nowhere near the code being changed; a worker who bumps the count but not the sorted list gets an array-diff failure that reads like an unrelated regression.
6. The split in step 3 must be behaviour-free. Run the daemon test leg at the end of that step, before any composition lands, or a move bug and a composition bug become one indistinguishable diff.
7. attempt-release-disposition.ts has ONE line of headroom against the 250 target. Any step that adds before the split has already broken the cap.
8. Mutation drills run in a shared worktree; snapshot hashes and restore by content, never `git checkout`.
